title: Install experience: match or beat hald/things-mcp (uvx-first, one-click, doctor, smooth upgrade)
description:
WHY: hald/things-mcp installs with one command (uvx things-mcp), one click (.mcpb), and a 3-line prereq list; ours currently offers four install options, verbose env config, a published wheel whose console script only works in editable installs (fixed on epic/hq-5wb, unreleased), and no single 'is it working?' step. Both servers read Things' SQLite via things.py, so hald's documented TCC failure (reads fail with 'unable to open database file' when Claude Desktop launches the server via its disclaimer helper; writes still work) applies to us and is undocumented here.
DESIGN: (1) uvx-first install story with .mcpb one-click and a claude-code one-liner; pip/venv/source preserved under Advanced. (2) A 'doctor' subcommand that verifies Things, Automation permission, DB readability (TCC), uv on PATH, and prints fixes — an improvement over hald, who has none. (3) A 'config' subcommand that prints (or safely writes) the client config so users never hand-edit JSON paths. (4) HTTP transport for parity and as the TCC fix ladder. (5) An explicit upgrade guide so existing venv/pip users keep working (things-mcp alias, python -m things_mcp) and can move to uvx when ready. (6) A PyPI release + .mcpb attach (human-executed) so uvx/.mcpb actually resolve.
CONSTRAINTS: no breaking changes for existing installs; Automation permission prompt is unavoidable (AppleScript writes) and must be documented, not hidden. Out of scope: bundling a full Python runtime in the .mcpb (uv-based bundle is more robust than relying on system python3).
BASE: build on epic/hq-k40 (which sits on epic/hq-5wb → origin/main v1.5.0).

title: Filter Someday-project tasks out of Today/Anytime/Upcoming (match Things UI)
description:
Why: things.py reports tasks inside a Someday project with their own start/anytime state, so get_today, get_anytime, get_upcoming (and get_todos activating-in-days variants) return items the Things UI hides. hald fixed this in v0.7.3 (src/things_mcp/server.py filter_someday_project_tasks + tests/test_someday_filtering.py) — reference that implementation.
Steps:
1. In src/things_mcp/tools_helpers/read_operations.py (or wherever get_today/get_anytime/get_upcoming build their lists), add a helper that loads the set of project UUIDs whose start == 'Someday' (things.projects(start='Someday')) once per call.
2. Drop any todo whose project (direct) OR whose heading's parent project is in that set from Today/Anytime/Upcoming/date-window results. Handle both 'project' and 'heading' membership — heading-parented todos do not carry the project UUID directly; resolve via the heading record.
3. get_someday must INCLUDE tasks belonging to Someday projects that things.py labels Anytime, and annotate them (e.g. an 'inherited_someday': true field or list label 'Someday (inherited from project)').
4. Edge cases: project missing/deleted → treat as not-Someday; todo with no project → keep; completed/canceled todos are out of scope for these views already.
5. Unit tests with mocked things.py data: task directly in Someday project, task under a heading in Someday project, task in Anytime project (control), standalone task (control). Cover today/anytime/upcoming/someday.
acceptance_criteria: get_today/get_anytime/get_upcoming exclude tasks in Someday projects (direct and via heading); get_someday includes them with an inherited marker; new unit tests pass; full pytest suite passes.

title: Diagnose & harden intermittent overnight cold-start MCP boot hang
description: Nightly llm-wiki sweep reports the things MCP server intermittently never completes the stdio handshake at overnight cold-start (60s connect timeout at 01:00Z on 2026-07-19/20; normal nights connect in 1.3-2.1s). Recurred May (hq-eww) and June (hq-h8v) in the consumer's tracker. Server-side stderr shows nothing, so the hang location is unknown. Code audit shows startup already avoids osascript (main.py:53-59 lazy probe fix) and _load_auth_token is file-only, so the cause is upstream of tool registration: interpreter/import stall, logging config, or module-level work. Design: (1) emit timestamped boot-phase markers to stderr from the first line of the entrypoint, (2) add a faulthandler-based startup watchdog that dumps all thread stacks to stderr if the server is not serving within a deadline, (3) audit the pre-handshake boot path for blocking I/O and file follow-ups, (4) release and advertise. OUT OF SCOPE: client-side mitigations (bump MCP_TIMEOUT in the sweep, gate connect-retry with backoff) live in llm-wiki's hq tracker, mirroring hq-0a3 for hermes.

title: get_someday: make Someday-project task inheritance OPT-IN via parameter (operator decision)
description:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-19: inheritance of tasks from Someday projects into get_someday must be opt-in. Live check on the maintainer's DB: raw get_someday = 570 items (77 native + 493 inherited from 28 Someday projects); under mode=standard the context manager truncates to ~110 and inherited items (appended last) fall off the page.
Steps:
1. In src/things_mcp/tools_helpers/read_operations.py _get_someday_sync / get_someday: add parameter include_project_tasks: bool = False. When False, return only things.someday() (pre-hq-5wb.1 behaviour). When True, also append inherited tasks marked inherited_someday=True (existing logic, keep dedup and defensive handling).
2. Thread the parameter through ThingsTools.get_someday and the MCP tool get_someday in server.py (Field description: 'Also include tasks that live inside Someday projects (marked inheritedSomeday=true). Default false; can be large.'). Keep _read_result shape.
3. Update unit tests in tests/unit/test_someday_filtering.py: default excludes inherited; include_project_tasks=True includes with marker; add server-level test via fastmcp.Client for both.
4. Docs: README + CLAUDE.md mention the parameter; CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased noting the hq-5wb.2 summary-mode count semantics (count=len(items), full count in total) as well.
5. Do NOT change Today/Anytime/Upcoming filtering — that stays always-on.
Also from reviewer notes (keep in scope only if trivial): get_areas summary yields items:[] because its preview key is 'areas' — pick it up in _read_result if a one-liner, otherwise leave.
acceptance_criteria: get_someday(include_project_tasks=False) returns only native Someday todos; =True adds inherited tasks with inheritedSomeday marker; unit + client tests cover both; docs + CHANGELOG updated; Today/Anytime/Upcoming filtering unchanged.
notes: Live check 2026-08-19: on the maintainer's DB get_someday raw = 570 items (77 native + 493 inherited from 28 Someday projects). Under mode=standard the context manager truncates to ~110 and inherited items are appended last, so fresh inherited todos fall off the page. Consider: interleave/sort inherited items with native ones, or make inheritance opt-in (include_project_tasks param).

title: Add add_area and update_area tools (AppleScript)
description:
Why: We have no way to create or rename an Area; hald added add_area/update_area in v0.8.1 via AppleScript (URL scheme has no add-area). We already use AppleScript for writes so this is a natural fit.
Steps:
1. In the AppleScript write layer, add add_area(title, tags=None) using 'make new area with properties {name:...}'; return the new area's id. Escape title with _escape_applescript_string().
2. Add update_area(id, title=None, tags=None): change only provided fields; tags replaces (comma-separated, existing-tags-only per project convention — filter non-existent tags silently like add_tags does).
3. Register both as MCP tools in server.py with docstrings/param descriptions; do NOT add delete_area (deleting an area deletes its projects — hald deliberately omitted it too).
4. Error handling: unknown area id → return {success:false, error:...} not an exception; empty title → validation error.
5. Unit tests with mocked AppleScript; manual check against real Things 3 per CLAUDE.md.
6. Advertise in README feature list and get_server_capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: add_area returns a real Things area id; update_area renames/re-tags only provided fields; errors are structured; tests pass; README + capabilities updated.

title: Migrate to FastMCP 3.x and return structured_content on read tools
description:
Why: pyproject pins fastmcp>=2.0.0 with no upper bound, so fresh installs may already resolve 3.x untested; installed here is 2.11.3. hald's v0.8.1 uses FastMCP 3.x ToolResult to return both human text and machine-readable structured_content (item dicts + count/total/offset/limit) on all read tools, so clients don't parse text. Reference hald src/things_mcp/server.py v0.8.1 for the ToolResult pattern.
Steps:
1. Bump pyproject.toml to fastmcp>=3.0.0,<4; run full pytest and fix breakage (3.x: @mcp.tool returns the original function — any tests using .fn must change).
2. For every read tool (get_inbox/today/upcoming/anytime/someday/logbook/trash/todos/projects/areas/tags/tagged_items/recent/search_todos/search_advanced/get_todo_by_id/get_due_in_days/get_activating_in_days), return a ToolResult whose content is the existing text output (unchanged) and whose structured_content is {items:[...], count, total, mode, limit, offset} with JSON-safe values (dates → ISO strings).
3. Response modes (summary/minimal/standard/detailed) must shape structured items the same way they shape text — do NOT ship full dicts under mode=summary (context-explosion risk noted in CLAUDE.md).
4. Update README/CLAUDE.md to advertise structured output.
5. Ambiguity flag: if FastMCP 3.x changes ctx/lifespan APIs used in server.py, note the diff in the bead rather than silently working around it.
acceptance_criteria: fastmcp>=3.0.0,<4 pinned; pytest green; every read tool returns text + structured_content; structured payload respects mode; docs updated.

title: Parity with hald/things-mcp: adopt its strongest features
description: Comparison (Aug 2026) of this server (v1.4.2) vs hald/things-mcp (v0.8.1, 557 stars, actively maintained). Both read via things.py; hald writes via URL scheme, we write via AppleScript. We lead on write power (delete/move/remove_tags), response modes, and date-window queries. hald leads on: FastMCP 3.x structured_content, Someday-project filtering in Today/Anytime/Upcoming, add_area/update_area, get_tag_usage, and .mcpb one-click packaging. These are the gaps most likely to make a user pick hald's server over ours. Each child bead closes one gap. Reference: https://github.com/hald/things-mcp and its CHANGELOG v0.7.3-v0.8.1.
close_reason: All 5 child beads reviewer-passed and squash-merged to epic/hq-5wb (rebased on origin/main v1.5.0)

title: Shield boot path from things.py's unbounded module-level Group Containers glob
description:
INPUT: src/things_mcp/tools.py:7 (`import things`) and src/things_mcp/tools_helpers/read_operations.py:8 (`import things`), which transitively trigger venv/.../site-packages/things/database.py:31-34:
  try:
      DEFAULT_FILEPATH = next(glob.iglob(os.path.expanduser(DEFAULT_FILEPATH_31616502)))
  except StopIteration:
      DEFAULT_FILEPATH = os.path.expanduser(DEFAULT_FILEPATH_31516502)
This module-level glob runs unconditionally, synchronously, and without a timeout the first time `things` is imported anywhere in the process -- which today happens at server import time (server.py -> tools.py), before ThingsMCPServer.__init__ even starts, and before most boot_marker phases fire. It walks ~/Library/Group Containers/JLMPQHK86H.com.culturedcode.ThingsMac/ThingsData-*/... on disk. If that path is slow to stat (external/synced volume asleep, FileVault unlock delay, Spotlight/mds or Time Machine snapshot contention around overnight hours), this call can block the entire stdio handshake indefinitely with zero stderr output -- this is a confirmed audit finding from hq-l1a.3, identified as the top hang hypothesis.

WORK:
1. In src/things_mcp/boot_trace.py or server.py, bracket the point where `things` first gets imported with boot_marker calls (e.g. `boot_marker("things-import-start")` / `boot_marker("things-import-done")`) so a future hang at this exact spot is visible in the boot trace even before the full fix lands.
2. Defer the first `import things` so it no longer executes synchronously on the module-import path that gates the stdio handshake: perform it lazily (first real use) inside a bounded operation, e.g. run the import via `asyncio.to_thread` (or a plain `threading.Thread` with `.join(timeout=...)` given this executes before any event loop exists in some call paths) with a hard timeout (a few seconds, configurable), and raise/log a clear diagnostic (not a silent hang) if the timeout is exceeded, rather than letting the client's 60s connect timeout be the only signal.
3. Do not change read/write behavior or the public ThingsTools/ReadOperations API -- only change *when* and *how safely* the `things` import happens.
4. Add a unit test (tests/unit) that simulates a slow `things` import (e.g. monkeypatch `importlib.import_module` or the glob call to sleep past the timeout) and asserts the server surfaces a clear timeout error/log line instead of hanging past the configured bound.
5. Run pytest tests/unit and confirm no regressions.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- The `things` import no longer runs unguarded on the synchronous critical path between process start and the stdio handshake being ready to serve.
- A bounded timeout (configurable, sane default e.g. 5-10s) surrounds the import/resolution, with a clear log/stderr message on timeout rather than silent hang.
- boot_trace markers bracket the import so future incidents are diagnosable even if the fix doesn't fully eliminate the underlying OS-level slowness.
- New unit test passes; full tests/unit suite passes with no regressions.
- No change to ThingsTools/ReadOperations public behavior when the import succeeds normally.

title: Add startup watchdog: dump all thread stacks if boot exceeds deadline
description: INPUT: src/things_mcp/main.py, src/things_mcp/server.py; builds on the boot-marker helper from hq-l1a.1. WORK: (1) Immediately after the process-start marker, arm Python's faulthandler: faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(timeout=20, repeat=True, file=sys.stderr) so that if boot stalls anywhere (imports, config, FastMCP init, handshake), every thread's stack is dumped to stderr every 20s — this is the diagnostic the 2026-07-20 outage lacked. (2) Cancel it (faulthandler.cancel_dump_traceback_later()) once the server reaches the point of calling self.mcp.run() AND re-arm is NOT done after that (mcp.run blocks for the server's lifetime by design; a lifetime repeat dump would spam stderr). Decision made here: cancel just before mcp.run() — boot is the window we instrument; if the hang is inside FastMCP's handshake after run() starts, the 20s repeat that fired before cancel still covers it only if cancel happens after handshake — so instead cancel from a FastMCP on-ready hook if available, else cancel after a one-shot 60s window (dump_traceback_later(60, repeat=False) armed at process start, no cancel needed). Implementer: prefer the simplest correct variant — one-shot 25s AND one-shot 55s dumps armed at process start, no cancellation needed; they are no-ops on healthy boots faster than 25s... except dump fires regardless of state; verify a healthy boot (connects in ~1.5s) does NOT emit dumps into normal operation logs in a way that breaks the MCP client — stderr is safe for stdio MCP servers (protocol uses stdout). Document the chosen variant in the bead notes. (3) Make deadline configurable via env THINGS_MCP_BOOT_WATCHDOG_SECS, default 25, 0 disables. EDGE CASES: stderr closed (wrap arm/cancel in try/except); faulthandler already enabled by env. DONE-CRITERIA: unit test that watchdog arms with default deadline, respects env override, and disables at 0; manual verification note that a normal server start still connects and, after the deadline passes with the server healthy, stderr traceback dumps (if any fire) do not corrupt MCP stdout; pytest tests/unit passes.

title: Add timestamped boot-phase markers to stderr from entrypoint
description: INPUT: src/things_mcp/main.py (main(), ServerManager.start), src/things_mcp/server.py (ThingsMCPServer.__init__, run), src/things_mcp/__main__.py. WORK: (1) At the very top of main() in main.py and of server.py main(), before any heavy import or config work, write a timestamped marker line directly to sys.stderr (unbuffered: print(..., file=sys.stderr, flush=True)) — do NOT rely on logging, which is configured later. (2) Emit markers at each boot phase: process-start (entrypoint reached), config-loaded, logging-configured, applescript-manager-ready, tools-registered, calling-mcp.run. Include ISO-8601 timestamp with milliseconds and elapsed-since-start in each line, prefix 'things-mcp boot:'. (3) Move heavy imports (server module, FastMCP) below the process-start marker if needed so the first marker fires within milliseconds of interpreter start — but keep public API/CLI behavior identical. EDGE CASES: stderr may be a pipe closed by the client — wrap marker writes in try/except OSError/ValueError like the existing stop() handlers. Markers must appear even when logging config later redirects/filters output. DONE-CRITERIA: running 'python -m things_mcp --version' still works; launching the server prints the process-start marker to stderr before FastMCP import completes; a unit test asserts the marker helper formats/flushes to stderr and swallows OSError; pytest tests/unit passes.

title: Audit pre-handshake boot path for blocking work; file follow-up beads
description: INPUT: everything executed before FastMCP serves the stdio handshake: src/things_mcp/__main__.py, main.py, server.py __init__/_configure_logging/_register_tools, services/applescript_manager.py __init__/_load_auth_token, tools.py ThingsTools.__init__ and every constructor it calls (PureAppleScriptScheduler, ValidationService, MoveOperationsTools, TagValidationService, ReadOperations, WriteOperations, BulkOperations, ResponseOptimizer, ContextAwareResponseManager, operation_queue, shared_cache), plus module-level statements in all imported things_mcp modules. WORK: enumerate every subprocess call, network call, file write, lock acquisition, or unbounded file read reachable during boot; check _configure_logging for file-handler paths that could block (e.g., log file on slow/locked volume); check for module-level osascript or 'import things' style side effects. Known-clean already (do not re-litigate, just confirm): lazy Things probe per main.py:53-59, _load_auth_token file-only reads. OUTPUT: findings written into this bead's notes as a table (call site -> blocking potential -> verdict), and one new bd task filed under epic hq-l1a per confirmed blocking call with a concrete fix. DONE-CRITERIA: notes contain the audit table covering every listed module; zero or more follow-up beads filed and linked; no code changes in this task.
notes:
## Pre-handshake boot path audit (hq-l1a.3)

| Call site (file:line) | Boot phase | Blocking potential | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `__main__.py:5-6` boot_marker/arm_boot_watchdog | process-start | stdlib only (time, os, sys, faulthandler) | CLEAN |
| `__main__.py:8` `from .main import main` | process-start -> import cascade | triggers transitive import of server.py -> tools.py -> `import things` (see below) | SUSPECT (carrier of the real issue) |
| `main.py:11-13` module imports (boot_trace, server, applescript_manager) | import cascade | same cascade as above | SUSPECT (carrier) |
| `main.py:21-25` `ServerManager.__init__` / `_setup_signal_handlers` | pre-config | `signal.signal()` only | CLEAN |
| `server.py:12-17` `from dotenv import load_dotenv; load_dotenv()` (module level) | import cascade | walks parent dirs from CWD looking for `.env` (bounded stat calls); could be slow if CWD is on a deep/slow/networked path, but bounded and typically sub-ms | CLEAN (low-risk) |
| `server.py:19` `from fastmcp import FastMCP` | import cascade | pulls in pydantic/uvicorn/httpx/mcp-sdk transitively; pure interpreter+import cost, no explicit I/O in our code, but cold-disk/cold-page-cache import of a large dependency tree can genuinely take seconds on an overnight-cold machine | CLEAN (code) / plausible EXTERNAL cause |
| `server.py:25` `from .tools import ThingsTools` -> `tools.py:7` `import things` -> `things/database.py:31-34` module-level `next(glob.iglob(os.path.expanduser(DEFAULT_FILEPATH_31616502)))` | import cascade (before any boot_marker fires except watchdog-armed) | **Unconditional, synchronous, unbounded filesystem glob** over `~/Library/Group Containers/JLMPQHK86H.com.culturedcode.ThingsMac/ThingsData-*/...` executed once at import time, on the same thread that must complete before `ThingsMCPServer.__init__` even starts. No timeout, no boot_marker bracketing it, not skippable via `THINGSDB` env var (that only affects `Database.__init__`, not this module-level constant). If `~/Library` is on a slow/locked/networked volume at cold overnight boot (external drive not yet mounted, FileVault unlock delay, Spotlight/mds or backup lock contention on Group Containers), this glob can stall indefinitely with zero stderr output — matches the reported symptom exactly. | **CONFIRMED-BLOCKING** |
| `services/applescript_manager.py:39-70` `AppleScriptManager.__init__` (incl. `_load_auth_token`, `AppleScriptExecutor()`, `AppleScriptFormatters()`, `AppleScriptQueries()`, `AppleScriptParser()`) | applescript-manager-ready | `_load_auth_token` is file-only reads of 3 candidate paths (KNOWN-CLEAN per brief); the 4 sub-constructors just set attributes, no I/O, no subprocess | CLEAN |
| `services/applescript/executor.py:24` `AppleScriptExecutor.__init__` | applescript-manager-ready | attribute assignment only; class-level `asyncio.Lock()` created at import (safe under Python 3.10+, no loop binding at creation) | CLEAN |
| `services/applescript/parser.py:62` `AppleScriptParser.__init__` | applescript-manager-ready | calls `reset()`, pure in-memory state | CLEAN |
| `services/applescript/formatters.py`, `queries.py` | applescript-manager-ready | no `__init__`, static/stateless methods | CLEAN |
| `tools.py:32` `ThingsTools.__init__` -> `PureAppleScriptScheduler`, `ValidationService`, `MoveOperationsTools`, `ResponseOptimizer`, `TagValidationService`, `ReadOperations`, `WriteOperations`, `BulkOperations` | tools-registered (pre) | all constructors (`pure_applescript_scheduler.py:42`, `services/validation_service.py:20`, `move_operations.py:22`, `response_optimizer.py:25`, `services/tag_service.py:32`, `tools_helpers/read_operations.py:20`, `tools_helpers/write_operations.py:20`, `tools_helpers/bulk_operations.py:20`) only store references/config; no subprocess, network, file I/O, or locks at construction | CLEAN |
| `tools_helpers/read_operations.py:8` `import things` (redundant transitive import, already loaded via tools.py) | import cascade | same module-level glob as above, already executed once (Python import cache) — no additional cost, but confirms the dependency is unconditional in two places | CLEAN (no additional cost; same root cause as above) |
| `context_manager.py:396` `ContextAwareResponseManager.__init__` (+ `SmartDefaultManager`, `ProgressiveDisclosureEngine`, `ResponseSizeEstimator`) | tools-registered (pre) | pure in-memory data structures | CLEAN |
| `server.py:96-132` `_configure_logging()` | logging-configured | Console `StreamHandler` used by default (`config.log_file_path is None`). **If** `THINGS_MCP_LOG_FILE_PATH` is set, does `Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` then `logging.FileHandler(path)` (blocking `open()`), with no timeout — could stall on a slow/locked/networked log directory (e.g. external volume asleep, log rotation holding a lock at 01:00). Confirmed via the actual deployed Claude Desktop config (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`) that `THINGS_MCP_LOG_FILE_PATH` is **not** set for this server today, so this path is currently inactive/unreached | CLEAN (as currently deployed) / SUSPECT (latent, only if ever configured) |
| `server.py:167` `_register_tools()` | tools-registered | Only defines/decorates async closures with `@self.mcp.tool()`; no tool body executes at registration time | CLEAN |
| `server.py:134-165` `_register_shutdown_handlers()` | tools-registered (post) | `atexit.register`, `signal.signal` only | CLEAN |
| `operation_queue.py` (`get_operation_queue`/global `_global_queue`) | not on boot path | Only instantiated lazily on first tool call (`queue_status`, bulk ops); never touched during `__init__` chain | CLEAN / not reachable at boot |
| `shared_cache.py` (fcntl locks, file I/O, `threading.RLock`) | not on boot path | grep confirms this module is never imported anywhere else in `things_mcp` — dead code, unreachable | CLEAN / not reachable |
| `locale_aware_dates.py:484` module-level `locale_handler = LocaleAwareDateHandler()` | import cascade | `__init__` only logs; no `locale.setlocale()` or I/O | CLEAN |
| `config.py` `load_config_from_env` -> `ThingsMCPConfig.from_env_file` | config-loaded | `Path(".env").exists()` stat (cheap) when no env_file given; pydantic `BaseSettings` reads `os.environ` only | CLEAN |
| main.py:53-59 lazy Things probe comment | n/a | confirmed absent from startup path as documented | CLEAN (confirmed, not re-litigated) |
| `services/applescript_manager.py:72-95` `_load_auth_token` | applescript-manager-ready | file-only reads of 3 fixed candidate paths | CLEAN (confirmed, not re-litigated) |

### Verdict counts
CLEAN: 20 · SUSPECT: 3 (import cascade carriers / latent file-logging path / cold fastmcp import) · CONFIRMED-BLOCKING: 1

### Conclusion (ranked hypotheses)
1. **Most plausible: the `things` library's module-level `glob.iglob()` over `~/Library/Group Containers/JLMPQHK86H.com.culturedcode.ThingsMac/ThingsData-*/...`**, executed unconditionally and synchronously the moment `import things` runs (transitively pulled in via `server.py -> tools.py`, before any of our own code executes and before most boot_markers fire). It has no timeout, cannot be bypassed via `THINGSDB` env var (that only affects `Database.__init__`, not this constant), and touches a filesystem location that plausibly stalls at overnight cold-start (external/synced volume asleep, FileVault unlock latency, Spotlight/mds or Time Machine local-snapshot contention on Group Containers around 01:00). This is a real, unbounded, blocking filesystem call reachable on every single boot, in third-party code we cannot edit in place but can shield ourselves from.
2. **Second: cold interpreter/import stall**, i.e. the sheer cost of importing `fastmcp` and its dependency tree (pydantic, httpx, uvicorn, mcp-sdk, etc.) on a machine where the page cache and/or disk have gone cold overnight (spun-down disk, first access after sleep, antivirus/Spotlight scanning newly-touched files). This is external to our code (no bug to fix) but is a legitimate contributor to intermittent multi-second-to-minute cold-start variance, and is indistinguishable from cause #1 without the boot markers/watchdog stack dump already added on this branch — which is exactly the right next diagnostic (a real overnight hang capture will show whether the watchdog fires during `import` before any marker, pointing at #1, or while genuinely inside `FastMCP`/`mcp.run()`, pointing elsewhere).
3. Third (much less likely given current deployment): the file-logging path in `_configure_logging()` is a real, unguarded blocking `open()` on a configurable path, but confirmed inactive in the actual deployed Claude Desktop config for this server today, so it cannot be the cause of the *currently observed* hangs — only a latent risk if a log file path is ever configured on a slow/networked volume.

No sqlite/db connections, subprocess/osascript spawns, or network calls were found anywhere on the boot path itself (the actual `sqlite3.connect()` inside `things.database.Database.__init__` and all `osascript` subprocess calls are correctly deferred to first tool invocation, matching the documented lazy-probe design).

value: bd init auto-commits its scaffolding (.beads/, AGENTS.md, .gitignore hunk) to whatever git branch is currently checked out. Always run bd init on main.
